Accretion (coastal management).subject: World Geography
Accretion (coastal management).question: What is Accretion (coastal management)? Process of coastal sediment returning to the visible portion of a beach.
Accretion (coastal management).fact: Accretion is the process of coastal sediment returning to the visible portion of a beach or foreshore after a submersion event.   A sustainable beach or foreshore often goes through a cycle of submersion during rough weather and later accretion during calmer periods.

Accretion (geology).subject: World Geography
Accretion (geology).question: What is Accretion (geology)? Geological process by which material is added to a tectonic plate at a subduction zone.
Accretion (geology).fact: In geology, accretion is a process by which material is added to a tectonic plate at a subduction zone, frequently on the edge of existing continental landmasses.   The added material may be sediment, volcanic arcs, seamounts, oceanic crust or other igneous features.

Accretionary wedge.subject: World Geography
Accretionary wedge.question: The _____ was Sediments at a convergent plate boundary.
Accretionary wedge.fact: An accretionary wedge or accretionary prism forms from sediments accreted onto the non-subducting tectonic plate at a convergent plate boundary. Most of the material in the accretionary wedge consists of marine sediments scraped off from the downgoing slab of oceanic crust, but in some cases the wedge includes the erosional products of volcanic island arcs formed on the overriding plate.

Accumulation zone.subject: World Geography
Accumulation zone.question: The _____ was Area on a glacier.
Accumulation zone.fact: On a glacier, the accumulation zone is the area above the firn line, where snowfall accumulates and exceeds the losses from ablation, (melting, evaporation, and sublimation). The accumulation zone is also defined as that part of a glacier's surface, usually at higher elevations, on which there is net accumulation of snow, which subsequently turns into firn and then glacier ice.
